title: Solubilities of Argon and Nitrogen in Sea Water
experimental_method: Microgasometric method (Douglas 1964) with an enlarged absorption apparatus (about 8 ml water); gas-free millipore-filtered sea water (vacuum extraction over mercury) equilibrated with pure Ar or N2; chlorinity by a scaled-down Mohr titration against Copenhagen water.
uncertainties_stated: Estimated accuracy +-0.25% for argon and +-0.5% for nitrogen; chlorinity +-0.05 o/oo; possible extra uncertainty up to 0.2% (Ar) and 0.4% (N2) from residual CO2 (text footnote 12).
quality_remarks: Chlorinity is g Cl per kg sea water; alpha is volume of gas (STPD) per unit volume of water at 760 mm gas pressure (wording of Table II footnote); volume of which water (sea water or solvent) and temperature scale not stated. Table I/III temperatures differ per column and per block. The Av. line is the authors' mean of the three replicate lines. Smoothed tables II and IV are not extracted. | audit 2026-10-02: the printed header reads 15.0 for the first temperature column of the Cl 15.376 block, but the N2 block of the same chlorinity (Table III) and the smoothed table show 1.50; the cells of that column (3 replicate rows and the Av. row) were changed from 15.0 to 1.50 in table_1.csv by coordinator decision. The seawater relation S = 1.80655 Cl used by the builder is not stated in the paper.
